title: Percentage increase and decrease
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:56Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches the same multiplier method, but it is broader than this Year 8 point because it adds reversing a percentage change and question b depends on that step, so no bank point fits as it stands or with small changes.

draft.title: Percentage increase and decrease
card: To change an amount by a percentage in one step, multiply by a single factor. The factor is the new amount as a decimal fraction of the original.
Add the percentage to 100%, then write it as a decimal. A 15% increase is 100% + 15% = 115%, so the factor is 1.15.
Take the percentage from 100%, then write it as a decimal. A 20% decrease is 100% − 20% = 80%, so the factor is 0.8.
Example: a $60 jacket rises in price by 15%. New price = 60 × 1.15 = $69.
draft.remember: Increase: 100% plus the change. Decrease: 100% minus the change. Then multiply.

a.why: A 30% decrease leaves 100% − 30% = 70%, which is 0.7. The factor 0.3 is tempting, but multiplying by 0.3 leaves only 30% of the amount, so it is a 70% decrease.
a.clue: Work out what percentage is left after the decrease.

b.q: Ravi's gym fee is $40 a week. It rises by 15%. What is the new weekly fee?
b.why: The factor is 1.15, so 40 × 1.15 = $46. The answer $6 is only the increase (15% of 40), not the new fee.
b.clue: The question asks for the new fee, not the size of the rise.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's facts and both answers check out (60 × 1.15 = 69, factor 0.7 for a 30% decrease, 40 × 1.15 = 46), and the explanations match the card.
